Full signed 14-bit ADC snapshots from actual failed PAC reads on a T5577,
Chameleon Ultra powered from a wall adapter and controlled through Android BLE.
Recorded 2026-11-23, firmware v2.3.26-cl diagnostic build, command 3014.

Each file is exactly 12288 little-endian int16 samples at 125 ksample/s,
three RF/32 PAC frame periods. No scaling, clipping, padding or splicing.
The buffers were copied immediately after the failed read, before the next
read or a fresh sniff could overwrite them. The input card identities are
generated test data, not access credentials.

pac-ble-failed-a1-pcm16.bin: cycle 1, read 1, ASCII ID 1234AB00.
pac-ble-failed-a2-pcm16.bin: cycle 2, read 1, ASCII ID 1234AB00.
pac-ble-failed-b-pcm16.bin: cycle 18, read 1, ASCII ID 1234AB01.
pac-ble-failed-c-pcm16.bin: v2.3.27-cl cycle 15, read 1, ASCII ID 1234AB02.
pac-ble-failed-a3-pcm16.bin: v2.3.27-cl cycle 44, read 2, ASCII ID 1234AB00.

The previous decoder's clipped/full-range hysteresis paths fail these complete
buffers. Short LC excursions reset its shift register; separately rounding
edge intervals also creates parity errors near a half-bit boundary. Filtering
short excursions and tracking fractional time across all 32 clock phases must
recover the exact ID at each of 32 acquisition offsets. Every candidate still
passes the original preamble, UART framing, odd parity and payload XOR checks.
The last two captures additionally need coherent median filtering of the
three physical frame periods. The acquisition regression exercises the actual
reader and raw buffers directly; no repeated capture, padding or synthesized
tail is involved in these PCM16 fixtures.
